entities.name: Theodorus of Asine
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Theodorus of Asine, a prominent Neoplatonist philosopher who flourished in the early 4th century CE and died around 360 CE, was a pivotal figure in the post-Iamblichean development of this intellectual tradition. Hailing from one of the Greek towns named Asine, most likely Asine in Laconia, he became a direct pupil and close associate of Iamblichus, the Syrian founder of the Apamean school of Neoplatonism. Theodorus's significance lies in his role as a crucial conduit for Iamblichus's complex philosophical system, particularly his metaphysics and theology, helping to codify and transmit these ideas to the next generation of thinkers in the late Roman Empire.

Theodorus was known for his extensive commentaries on Plato and Aristotle, though regrettably, most of his original works are lost, surviving primarily through fragments and mentions in later Neoplatonic authors like Proclus. He engaged deeply with the intricate Neoplatonic hierarchies, particularly concerning the nature of the One, Intellect, Soul, and the sensible world, often clarifying or elaborating upon Iamblichus's sometimes obscure doctrines. His philosophical contributions included a refined theory of the Forms and their relation to the divine intellect, alongside detailed expositions on the structure of the cosmos and the human soul's ascent towards the divine.

The legacy of Theodorus of Asine is most evident in his profound influence on later Neoplatonists, particularly Syrianus, the teacher of Proclus, who frequently cited and engaged with Theodorus's interpretations. Through this intellectual lineage, Theodorus's understanding of Iamblichus's system became integrated into the foundational texts of the Athenian Neoplatonic school, ensuring his ideas continued to shape philosophical discourse for centuries. His role underscores the interconnectedness of late antique philosophical schools and the critical importance of pupils in transmitting and refining their masters' teachings.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Theodorus of Asine played a crucial role in the transmission and interpretation of Iamblichean Neoplatonism, directly influencing later prominent philosophers like Syrianus and Proclus and shaping the trajectory of late antique philosophy.
